literal: To do difficult things those who do are great people; small people are those who do not do things difficult to do.
translation: Great are those who achieve deeds that are difficult to perform; those who cannot accomplish such difficult deeds are small.
modern: செய்வதற்கு அரிய செயல்களைச் செய்பவர்கள் பெரியவர்கள்; செய்ய முடியாதவர்கள் சிறியவர்கள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts great individuals with lesser ones based on their capacity to perform difficult deeds. The author defines greatness not by birth or status, but by the ability to accomplish tasks that seem impossible to ordinary people. Those who shrink from difficult tasks and fail to perform them are deemed small or ordinary. The repetition of the phrase 'செயற்கு அரிய' (difficult to do) emphasizes that the true measure of a person's stature is the magnitude of the challenges they overcome.
